'''Joseph Laws McKibben''' (1912 &ndash; 2001) was an [[Americans|American]] [[physicist]] and [[engineer]] who worked with [[J. Robert Oppenheimer]] as a group leader on the [[Manhattan Project]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.osti.gov/opennet/manhattan-project-history/publications/LANLMDHProjectYPart2.pdf|title=Manhattan District History, Project Y, The Los Alamos Project|website=U.S. Department of Energy Office of Scientific and Technical Information}}</ref> He personally witnessed the [[Trinity (nuclear test)|Trinity test]] and  flipped the switches that activated the timers that set off the atomic bomb at Trinity.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.atomicheritage.org/profile/joe-mckibben|title=Joe McKibben, Scientist, Trinity Site, Los Alamos, NM, Manhattan Project Veteran, Scientist, Trinity Test Eyewitness|website=Atomic Heritage Foundation}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Rhodes |first=Richard |author-link=Richard Rhodes |title=The Making of the Atomic Bomb |title-link=The Making of the Atomic Bomb |location=New York |publisher=Simon & Schuster |year=1986 |isbn=0-671-44133-7 |oclc=13793436}}</ref> 

McKibben, motivated by his daughter Karan's paralysed hands due to [[polio]], also invented the [[Pneumatic artificial muscles|Air Muscle]] in 1957.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Gurstelle |first=William |date=21 May 2015 |title=Making a Simple Air Muscle - A father's love inspired this A-bomb maker to invent a pneumatic actuator that's used in robots today. |url=https://makezine.com/projects/make-40/joseph-mckibben-and-the-air-muscle/ |magazine=Makezine |location=Santa Rosa, California, USA |publisher= Make.co |access-date= 4 April 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Gurstelle |first=William |author-link=William Gurstelle |date=1 Feb 2017 |title=ReMaking History, Volume 3: Makers of the Modern World |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=P31VDgAAQBAJ |location=Canada |publisher=Maker Media, Inc., 1160 |page= Chapter 9, Joseph McKibben and the Air Muscle|isbn=9781680450682 }}</ref>

He was born in 1912 in [[Missouri]]. He died in 2001 in [[Los Alamos, New Mexico|Los Alamos]], aged 89.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://peoplelegacy.com/joseph_laws_mckibben-271p2.|title=Joseph Laws McKibben|website=PeopleLegacy.com}}</ref> His remains, and those of his wife and daughter, were interred at Guaje Pines Cemetery in Los Alamos. <ref> https://www.interment.net/data/us/nm/los-alamos/guaje-pines/index.htm</ref>
